top_cited_works.title: Growth model interpretation of planet size distribution
top_cited_works.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
top_cited_works.abstract: Significance The discovery of numerous exoplanet systems containing diverse populations of planets orbiting very close to their host stars challenges the planet formation theories based on the solar system. Here, we focus on the planets with radii of 2–4 R ⊕ , whose compositions are debated. They are thought to be either gas dwarfs consisting of rocky cores embedded in H 2 -rich gas envelopes or water worlds containing significant amounts of H 2 O-dominated fluid/ice in addition to rock and gas. We argue that these planets are water worlds.
